subscription.usage_cap_note: Owner 2026-11-19: 'do not exceed 90% of usage on any account.' run_sub.py's UsageCap sends a question only if every usage window (five_hour, seven_day, and a model's own window) stays at or under max less margin with every reply still running, and this one, counted at the most a reply can cost; otherwise it waits for the window's reset or a /login. Every such window needs a reading from the last reading_max_age_min; a missing one is read by a one-word probe first. margin 0.05 leaves room for interactive Claude Code use of the same account, which the solver cannot see until its next reading; margin_by_window gives the five-hour window 0.2 (the solver stops at 0.70 there), as heavy interactive work (source imports) can use 0.03 of it in ten minutes, while the weekly windows still reach 0.85. reply_max_usd: a reply that runs to the 128k output token limit (Fable 5.2 about $27.8 per million output tokens, Opus 5.5 about $21.3, measured on the POTD replies). prior_per_usd: usage per USD of reply cost until the readings tell (one account, 2026-11-19: 0.0215 of five_hour per USD, 0.0022 of seven_day, 0.0044 of the Fable window; the priors are higher, to be safe on an account with a smaller plan). Simulated on the POTD Fable replies at margin 0.01, 1000 five-hour windows ended at 0.82 on average and never above 0.885. reply_cost_scale (owner 2026-11-20: 'scale the cost estimate to 0.75x', then 'Set the scale to 0.5'): a running reply is counted at that fraction of its worst case (reply_max_usd or the dearest reply seen), so more run at once. The cap then holds only for replies that cost at most twice the scaled figure on average: if every reply running at once did reach the full worst case, a window could end at (plan - u) / scale + u, e.g. five_hour 1.40 from a fresh window or 0.90 from 0.50 (cut-offs at the output limit: 11 of 3,274 POTD replies to 2026-11-20).

usage_cap.reply_cost_scale_note: 2026-11-24 21:10 (owner: 'it feels like we're not getting the maximum throughput'): 0.5 -> 0.25. A running reply is counted at reply_max_usd x this until it ends: $0.70 for Opus, $0.90 for Fable, still above the dearest reply seen ($0.48 over 2,000; median $0.06). At 0.5 an account dropped below 10 replies at once from about 52% of its five-hour window (the stop is 0.70), and the workers were busy about 62% of the time in the tie-break run; the five-hour margin (0.20 below the 0.90 cap) is unchanged.
